previousCoordinate.reasonReplaced: Legacy-punktet lå omtrent 3,06 kilometer nord-nordøst ved Spydeberg tettsted og identifiserte ikke prestegården eller det fredede 1814-anlegget.

identity.resolvedIdentity: Spydeberg prestegårds fredede hovedbygning, der Christian Frederik holdt statsråd 8. august 1814.
identity.identityProblem: Navnet kan vise til hovedbygningen, hele prestegårdstunet, den rekonstruerte Wilse-hagen, stiftelsen eller et generelt prestegårdsområde. 1814-stedet må forankres i hovedbygningen uten å redusere det større fredede anlegget til ett punkt.
identity.splitReason: Hovedbygningen er 1814-ankeret. Tunet, stabburet og hagen inngår som sekundært anleggskontekst i samme place-record.

evidence.finding: Commons identifies Spydeberg prestegård as a protected rectory and museum at approximately 59.59067, 11.07696; monument photographs identify Norwegian heritage ID 86078.
evidence.reason: Combines the mapped entity with the official national heritage identifier for the rectory.

evidence.finding: The article places the rectory approximately three kilometres south of Spydeberg, gives site coordinate 59.59093, 11.07714, identifies the protected main building, storehouse, yard and garden, and documents the 8 August 1814 council meeting.
evidence.reason: Provides an independent whole-site coordinate approximately 30.6 metres from the applied main-building point and confirms the event identity.

evidence.sourceName: Visit Indre Østfold / Visit Norway – Spydeberg prestegård
evidence.finding: The visitor listing gives Giltvetveien 18 and describes the protected main building, storehouse and garden, the 1814 meeting and guided access.
evidence.reason: Confirms the current visit identity and address while the heritage entity supplies the spatial anchor.

evidence.finding: Riksantikvaren documents the 1991 protection, the reconstructed Wilse garden and the 8 August 1814 council meeting in the main house.
evidence.reason: Authoritatively confirms protection, building-and-garden context and the event.

evidence.finding: The foundation's purpose is to manage the rectory as a national memorial and communicate the Enlightenment, Wilse and the events of 8–9 August 1814.
evidence.reason: Confirms the current heritage-management identity and interpretive scope.

evidence.finding: The legacy coordinate lies approximately 3,056.2 metres north-northeast of the protected rectory.
evidence.reason: Rejected because it does not identify the rectory, main building or protected site.

addressCandidates.rejectionReason: The address confirms identity and access, while the heritage entity point more directly identifies the main historic building.

sourceObjectCandidates.rejectionReason: The coordinate is retained as a whole-site control rather than the main-building anchor.
A road-address point may identify access rather than the 1814 room-bearing main building.
The settlement is approximately three kilometres north and is not the historic site.

rawEvidence.description: Persisted heritage identity, main-building and whole-site coordinates, 1814 event evidence, visitor address, Wilse garden context and access limitations.

decision.nextAction: Applied the protected main-building point, retained the whole rectory site as a secondary anchor and continued with tistedalen_saugbrugsforeningen.

notes: The coordinate moves approximately 3,056.2 metres south-southwest.
The marker represents the main rectory building where the 8 August 1814 council meeting took place.
The protected storehouse, yard and reconstructed Wilse garden are part of the wider site context.
The Constitution was adopted at Eidsvoll and the Convention of Moss was concluded in Moss; Spydeberg is the council and headquarters site in the intervening crisis.
The radius is not a building, garden, heritage, property or event boundary, and opening and access rules apply.
